Which of the following statements are logically equivalent?

I. $X∧¬Y$

II. $¬(Y∨¬X)$

III. $¬Y∧(X∨X)$
questions.worked_solution:
Two statements are logically equivalent if they have the same truth table. So, we construct a truth table for the three given statements:

| $\,X\,$ | $\,Y\,$ | $\,X∧¬Y\,$ | $\,¬(Y∨¬X)\,$ | $\,¬Y∧(X∨X)\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |

We see that all three statements have the same truth table, so they are logically equivalent.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I, II, and III."

Find the missing values in the following truth table:

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,¬(A∧B)\,$ | $\,¬A∨¬B\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-1}} |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-2}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-3}} | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |

Using your results, complete the following statement:

$$
¬(A∧B){{field-4}}¬A∨¬B
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's solve for the missing values:

- When $A≡\text{T}$ and $B≡\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}¬A∨¬B & ≡¬\text{T}∨¬\text{T} \\  & ≡\text{F}∨\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $A≡\text{T}$ and $B≡\text{F},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}¬A∨¬B & ≡¬\text{T}∨¬\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}∨\text{T} \\  & ≡\text{T}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $A≡\text{F}$ and $B≡\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(A∧B) & ≡¬(\text{F}∧\text{T}) \\  & ≡¬\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{T}\end{aligned}
$$

Our completed table is shown below.

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,¬(A∧B)\,$ | $\,¬A∨¬B\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |

To determine whether $¬(A∧B)$ is logically equivalent to $¬A∨¬B,$ we need to check whether their truth tables are equivalent.

Looking at the last two columns, we see that they are the same $(\text{F},\text{T},\text{T},\text{T}).$ Therefore, we conclude that 

$$
¬(A∧B)≡¬A∨¬B.
$$

questions.worked_solution:
First, let's solve for the missing values:

- When $A≡\text{T}$ and $B≡\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(A∧B)∨¬(A∨¬B) & ≡(\text{T}∧\text{T})∨¬(\text{T}∨¬\text{T}) \\  & ≡(\text{T}∧\text{T})∨¬(\text{T}∨\text{F}) \\  & ≡\text{T}∨¬\text{T} \\  & ≡\text{T}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $A≡\text{T}$ and $B≡\text{F},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(A∧B)∨¬(A∨¬B) & ≡(\text{T}∧\text{F})∨¬(\text{T}∨¬\text{F}) \\  & ≡(\text{T}∧\text{F})∨¬(\text{T}∨\text{T}) \\  & ≡\text{F}∨¬\text{T} \\  & ≡\text{F}∨\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $A≡\text{F}$ and $B≡\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(A∧B)∨¬(A∨¬B) & ≡(\text{F}∧\text{T})∨¬(\text{F}∨¬\text{T}) \\  & ≡\text{F}∨¬\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}∨\text{T} \\  & ≡\text{T}\end{aligned}
$$

Our completed table is shown below.

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,(A∧B)∨¬(A∨¬B)\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |

To determine whether $(A∧B)∨¬(A∨¬B)$ is logically equivalent to $A,$ we need to check whether their truth tables are equivalent.

We see that the columns for $(A∧B)∨¬(A∨¬B)$ and $A$ are different. They differ in the second and third rows. Therefore, we conclude that 

$$
(A∧B)∨¬(A∨¬B)≢A.
$$
